follow_up_questions: How long have you had this pain - hours, days, or weeks?
Is the pain constant or does it come and go?
Does it hurt more with hot or cold foods or drinks?
Is there any swelling in your jaw or face?
Do you see any visible cavity, crack, or bleeding?

minor_cavity.description: A small cavity that needs to be cleaned and filled.

deep_cavity.description: The decay has reached the nerve. A root canal removes the infected pulp.

tooth_abscess.treatment: Emergency drainage plus antibiotics and possible extraction
tooth_abscess.description: An abscess is a dangerous bacterial infection. If untreated it can spread to the jaw or brain.

tooth_extraction.description: The tooth is too damaged to be saved and needs removal.

follow_up_questions: Where exactly is the pain - front, back, or one side?
Is it a throbbing pain or a pressure and tightness feeling?
Do you have nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light?
Did the headache come on suddenly or gradually?
Have you had any recent head injury or fever?

tension_headache.treatment: Rest, hydration, OTC pain reliever such as paracetamol
tension_headache.description: Common stress or tension headache - usually resolves with rest.
tension_headache.see_doctor_within: Only if it persists more than 3 days

migraine.treatment: Migraine medication, dark room rest, neurologist referral
migraine.description: A migraine episode - consult a doctor for proper medication.

severe_sudden_headache.treatment: Emergency CT scan and hospital admission
severe_sudden_headache.description: Sudden severe headache may indicate a brain bleed. This is life-threatening.

follow_up_questions: What is your temperature reading if you have a thermometer?
How many days have you had the fever?
Do you have any other symptoms such as cough, rash, or pain?
Have you travelled recently or been around sick people?
Are you able to drink fluids and stay hydrated?

mild_fever.treatment: Rest, fluids, paracetamol to manage temperature
mild_fever.description: Mild fever - likely a minor viral infection. Monitor at home.
mild_fever.see_doctor_within: Only if fever persists beyond 3 days

high_fever.treatment: Doctor visit - may need blood tests or antibiotics
high_fever.description: High or persistent fever needs professional evaluation.

critical_fever.description: Extremely high fever with neurological symptoms may indicate meningitis or sepsis.

follow_up_questions: Is the chest pain sharp, pressure-like, or burning?
Does the pain spread to your arm, neck, or jaw?
Are you short of breath or feeling dizzy?
Did it start during exercise or at rest?
Do you have a history of heart problems?

acid_reflux.description: Likely acid reflux or GERD - manageable with medication and diet.

possible_heart.treatment: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES - possible heart attack
possible_heart.description: These symptoms can indicate a heart attack. Do not drive yourself. Call for help immediately.
possible_heart.see_doctor_within: CALL 1990 Sri Lanka or emergency services NOW
